classic.aim: Be the first to play every tile on your rack. There are 106 tiles: 1 to 13 in four colours, two of each, and two jokers. Everyone starts with 14.
classic.sets: Tiles go on the table in sets of three or more. A run is one colour, numbers in a row (1 comes before 2, never after 13). A group is one number in three or four different colours.
classic.turn: Put tiles from your rack on the table, as new sets or added to sets already there, then press {{endTurn}}. If you can’t play, or would rather not, press {{draw}}: you take a tile and your turn ends.
classic.turnCaption: The blue 3 extends the run, and the red 8 joins the group.
classic.first: Your first sets must come from your rack alone and be worth 30 points or more together. A tile is worth its number; a joker, the tile it stands for.
classic.firstCaption: A red 10, 11 and 12 make 33 points: enough to start.
classic.table: After your first play, you can rearrange every set on the table: split them, take tiles from them, move tiles between them. When your turn ends, every set must be valid again and at least one tile must have come from your rack.
classic.splitCaption: Splitting a run to fit in a second red 6.
classic.borrowCaption: Taking the blue 4 from a group of four to make a run.
classic.joker: A joker stands in for any tile. Swap in the tile it stands for and you can take the joker, but you must use it again in the same turn.
classic.jokerCaption: The black 3 takes the joker’s place, and the joker joins the orange 5 and 6.
classic.end: The game ends when someone plays their last tile. Everyone else loses the points left on their rack (a joker costs 30), and the winner gains them all. If no tiles are left to draw and nobody can play, the lowest rack wins.
classic.controlsDrag: Drag tiles from your rack onto the table, or double-click a tile to play it.
classic.controlsSets: Drag a set by its handle on the left to move it around the table.
classic.controlsPlans: While others play, build your next sets in the strip above your rack.
classic.controlsReset: {{reset}} puts back everything you changed this turn.
classic.controlsTime: Watch the clock: when time runs out, what you’ve played that makes a valid turn stays, and the rest goes back to your rack.

okeyShared.indicator: At the deal one tile is turned up: the indicator. The tile one higher in its colour is the okey (after 13 comes 1). Both okeys are wild: each can stand for any tile, and the board rings them in gold. The two false okeys aren’t wild: each stands for the okey’s own tile.
okeyShared.indicatorCaption: With a red 4 as the indicator, the red 5s are the okeys, and the false okeys count as red 5s.

okey101.controlsDraw: Press {{draw}} or the pool to draw. To take the previous player’s discard, drag it onto your rack (or straight onto the table); drag it back if you change your mind.
okey101.aim: Okey 101 is played over several hands (7 unless the room chose otherwise), and the lowest total of penalty points wins. In each hand, be the first to go out. There are 106 tiles: 1 to 13 in four colours, two of each, and two false okeys. The player who starts gets 22 tiles, everyone else 21.
okey101.sets: A run is three or more tiles of one colour, numbers in a row (1 comes before 2, never after 13). A group is one number in three or four different colours. A pair is two identical tiles. An okey can take the place of any tile in a set.
okey101.turn: Draw a tile from the pool ({{draw}}), or take the tile the player before you just discarded, if it goes on the table this turn. Then lay down sets or add to the table, if you can, and end your turn by putting one tile on your discard spot. The player who starts only discards.
okey101.turnCaption: Having opened, you take the blue 7 the player before you discarded, add it and the blue 8 to the run, and discard the orange 2.
okey101.open: Your first sets must come from your rack and be worth 101 points or more together: a tile is worth its number, an okey the tile it stands for. Or open with five pairs. Until you open you can’t add to the table. Open with pairs and you lay down only pairs from then on, though you may still add to the runs and groups on the table. With {{rising}}, each opening must beat the one before it in the hand.
okey101.openCaption: A run and two groups: 106 points, enough to open.
okey101.add: Once you’ve opened, you can add tiles to the ends of any run or group on the table, yours or someone else’s, at most two at each end of a run in a turn. Sets are never rearranged, and pairs can’t be added to. From the turn after you opened, you can take an okey from the table by putting the tile it stands for in its place; from a group, only once the group has all four colours.
okey101.addCaption: The blue 3 and 7 go on the ends of the run; the red 9 takes the okey’s place in the group, and the okey comes to your rack.
okey101.penalties: With {{penalties}} on (as rooms start), some moves cost 101 points: discarding an okey, discarding a tile that could go on a set on the table (unless it’s your last), and having an okey taken from a set you laid down. If the next player opens with your discard, you pay its number times 10, or times 20 if they open with pairs.
okey101.out: To go out, lay down every tile but one and discard that last one. The hand ends there, and you score −101.
okey101.outCaption: The last sets go down and the last tile is discarded: the hand is over.
okey101.scores: A player who never opened scores 202. One who opened scores the numbers left on their rack (double if they opened with pairs), plus 101 for each okey. Everything doubles if the last discard was an okey, and doubles again if the winner opened with pairs, or opened and went out in one turn before anyone else had opened. Opening with 150 points or seven pairs earns −101. If the pool runs out, racks are scored the same way, without a winner, if anyone had opened; if everyone opens with pairs, the hand is dealt again.
okey101.controlsSets: Drop tiles on a set on the table to add them at its nearer end, or on the empty space to start a new set.
okey101.controlsDiscard: Drop a tile on your discard spot to end your turn. Until then, tiles you put down this turn can be moved again, and {{reset}} takes them all back.
okey101.controlsTime: Watch the clock: when time runs out, you draw if you hadn’t, what you laid down is played if it’s valid, and a tile that costs no penalty is discarded for you.

okey.controlsDraw: Press {{draw}} or the pool to draw. To take the previous player’s discard, drag it onto your rack; drag it back if you change your mind.
okey.aim: Be the first to make your rack a winning hand. There’s no table: everything happens on your rack. There are 106 tiles: 1 to 13 in four colours, two of each, and two false okeys. The player who starts gets 15 tiles, everyone else 14.
okey.hand: All 14 tiles in runs and groups, each tile in one set, or seven pairs of identical tiles. A run is three or more tiles of one colour, numbers in a row; 12 13 1 counts, 13 1 2 doesn’t. A group is one number in three or four different colours. An okey can stand in for any tile.
okey.handCaption: A winning hand: two runs, a group, and a run with the okey as the orange 4.
okey.turn: Draw a tile from the pool ({{draw}}), or take the tile the player before you just discarded. Then discard one tile onto your discard spot, leaving 14 on your rack. The player who starts only discards.
okey.turnCaption: You take the orange 6 the player before you discarded, for the orange 4 and 5, and discard the black 2.
okey.finish: When your other 14 tiles make a winning hand, put your last tile on the finish spot in the middle instead of discarding it. Your hand is shown to everyone, and the hand is over.
okey.scores: Everyone starts with 20 points (unless the room chose otherwise). When someone finishes, each other player loses 2, or 4 if the winner finished with an okey or with seven pairs, 8 for both. Holding the indicator’s twin at the deal shows it and costs each other player 1. If the pool runs out, the hand is dealt again. The game ends when someone has no points left: the most points win.
okey.controlsDiscard: Drop a tile on your discard spot to end your turn, or on the finish spot to win with the other 14. Sort your rack with the buttons above it, or drag tiles into your own order.
okey.controlsTime: Watch the clock: when time runs out, you draw if you hadn’t, and a tile is discarded for you.
